# GEO report: orchard-site **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 100/100, Strong Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. Every applicable rule is clear, judged from reading the code. I read all five files under `app/` and both files in `public/`, plus `geo.config.json`. The one thing code can't show is whether a CDN or firewall blocks real crawlers. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first Nothing is broken. The biggest unknown is the one the code can't settle. ### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your host - **Why it matters:** a CDN or firewall can block search crawlers even when `robots.txt` allows them, and the code can't show that. - **Where:** outside the repository (hosting or CDN settings) - **What the code says:** `public/robots.txt:1`: `User-agent: *` followed by `Allow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** stays at 100. The check confirms the result but isn't scored. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, 11 valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access you declared | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-3` allows `*` except `/account`. Policy is `allow`. | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Clear | Not run | `/`, `/varieties` and `/visit` have no noindex. Only `/account` does (`app/account/page.tsx:1`). | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your own domain | Clear | Not run | `app/page.tsx:1`, `app/varieties/page.tsx:1`, `app/visit/page.tsx:1` (3 of 3 routes) | | GEO-003 | Content is in server HTML | Clear | Not run | Server Components in the Next.js App Router, with no client-only fetching | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and robots.txt points to it | Clear | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml`, and `public/robots.txt:11` | | GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:5` has `lang="en"`. All 3 routes have a title and description. | | GEO-016 | Key pages reachable by normal links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:7` uses `` for all three pages | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions against AI search | Clear | Not run | Only a scoped `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:9`. No page-wide nosnippet or header config. | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | Read `app/layout.tsx` and the 3 main pages. There are no images, and the nav links have text. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | `llms.txt` (informational) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. This is not scored and not a problem. | | GEO-102 | App structured data (informational) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app | ## Other problems found None found. ## Worth considering - **Visit page promises directions but gives none:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Opening times and directions.'`, and the body is `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.` Add an address, directions and hours as text. Once those are visible, `LocalBusiness` structured data could label them, which might help readers and machines. - **Varieties are a single sentence:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`: `Over forty varieties, from Ashmead’s Kernel to Worcester Pearmain.` The page names two of the forty. A list, with each variety on its own page and URL, would answer what visitors come to ask and might give machines more to quote. - **Sitemap has no dates:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `https://www.orchard.example/`. Adding `` could give crawlers a freshness signal, but only if you have real update dates. - **Home page links only to two pages:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `

Grown in Herefordshire since 1952.

`. Links to varieties and visiting from the page body, not just the nav, might help readers move on. You deliberately block `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` (`public/robots.txt:5-9`), which matches your `trainingCrawlers: "block"` policy. I counted nothing against it. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Status codes and headers:** whether the server returns 200 for each page, and any `X-Robots-Tag` header added outside the repository, need a live check. ## Assumptions - You want search and AI search tools to find the public pages. `geo.config.json` says so with `aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`. - The `/account` page is meant to stay private. It has noindex, is disallowed in `robots.txt`, and isn't in the sitemap or the nav. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command for any item you adopt. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
